downtown-savannah-ga.name: Downtown Savannah
downtown-savannah-ga.title: Historic masonry and foundation work downtown
downtown-savannah-ga.summary: Check the historic-district review route and document masonry before choosing a structural repair or cosmetic repointing.
cards: Check the preservation guidance

The Chatham County–Savannah Metropolitan Planning Commission publishes a masonry repointing policy for the Downtown Savannah Historic District, alongside building-documentation guidance. Check the property designation and ask preservation staff which review applies to the proposed exterior work.
https://www.thempc.org/Historic/Pai
MPC historic-district policies
Separate a mortar repair from support movement

Before covering a crack, record its location, width and date, and compare nearby floors, openings and accessible supports. Repointing a joint does not establish that movement has stopped. Likewise, an old crack alone is not evidence that the house needs new piers.
Plan the repair around existing finishes

Ask how the proposed work protects masonry, plaster and utility connections. Record inaccessible areas and agree on a realistic adjustment target. Include lane access and material handling in the scope so the support repair and restoration work can be priced separately.
downtown-savannah-ga.next: Use measured movement and the condition of the masonry to decide what a crack-repair proposal needs to address.

midtown-savannah-ga.name: Midtown Savannah
midtown-savannah-ga.title: Midtown drainage: what Casey South can tell you
midtown-savannah-ga.summary: Use the Casey South drainage project as local context while tracing the actual water path at your property.
cards: A documented drainage project nearby

Savannah’s Casey South project includes drainage improvements along 54th, 56th and 57th streets, with work described between Atlantic, Harmon and Abercorn. The city project updates provide local drainage context; they do not diagnose a particular home or guarantee that its yard will stay dry.
https://www.savannahga.gov/3911/Latest-Updates-Page
City of Savannah Casey South updates
Record where water enters the property

From a safe, dry position after rain, photograph downspout discharge, yard low spots and the crawl-space entrance. Note whether the problem starts during rainfall or persists afterward. Share dates and earlier observations rather than attributing all dampness to a nearby street project.
Match the work to the observed problem

Standing water, humid air and damaged timber require separate checks. Establish the source and a suitable discharge route before specifying drainage equipment. Inspect joists and bearings where the floor has softened; a membrane by itself does not repair weakened framing.
midtown-savannah-ga.next: If the floor changes when the crawl space becomes wet, ask for a support inspection alongside the moisture assessment.

pooler-ga.name: Pooler
pooler-ga.title: Pooler flood records and a property-level repair plan
pooler-ga.summary: Find available elevation records, distinguish flood information from settlement evidence and separate driveway work from structural repair.
cards: Check records for the exact address

Pooler’s flood-protection page lists flood-map resources and elevation certificates by street and lot, including entries on Governor Treutlen Circle and Arbor Village Drive. Look for the actual property record and confirm the effective map with the city; a nearby listing is not a substitute.
https://www.pooler-ga.gov/resources/flood-protection/
Pooler flood resources and elevation certificates
Flood elevation is not a settlement diagnosis

An elevation certificate and a floor-level survey answer different questions. Bring any existing certificate, building plans and repair records to the inspection, but use current measurements and the support condition to evaluate movement. A flood-zone label does not determine pier depth or repair quantity.
Identify which concrete has moved

Mark whether the crack or drop is in a driveway, garage apron or load-bearing part of the building. Ask the inspector to check panel condition, nearby runoff and visible erosion. A sound independent panel may have different repair options from a moving foundation.
A local soil series, not a city-wide diagnosis

USDA established the Pooler soil series in Chatham County and records a type location in the Port Wentworth quadrangle. Its description identifies poor drainage and slow permeability. The name does not establish that a Pooler house sits on this soil: check the mapped unit and investigate the actual footing conditions.
https://soilseries.sc.egov.usda.gov/OSD_Docs/P/POOLER.html
USDA official Pooler soil-series description
pooler-ga.next: For a driveway or walkway issue, compare lifting suitability, drainage correction and replacement before choosing the scope.
